judgement.missedOpportunity: The tonal-blue grown-up version of the cobalt skirt. Pair s34 with s08 (light blue oversized shirt), half-tucked with sleeves rolled, plus s56 (silver pointed flats), s65 (silver watch) and s62 (straw tote). It wears colour on colour in her flattering cool blues and uses only silver metals for her undertone. It brings in the never-worn skirt and the once-worn shoe at the same time, so it is a real surprise that still reads quiet and Toteme. A close second is genuinely splitting the co-ord: s17 worn open over s13 with s34 and s53.
judgement.summary: This is a solid, client-aware set that reaches for exactly the right under-used pieces: the cobalt skirt s34, the sage co-ord s17/s27, the navy tailoring s30 and the silver flats s56. Look 1 is the standout and a genuine answer to 'surprise me'. Look 2 is weather-perfect but less inventive than its copy claims. Look 3 is a smart office outfit with muddled metals and little surprise. The explanations contain small inaccuracies: cobalt is not 'near your face', and the co-ord is not actually 'broken up'. The gold-heavy jewellery repeats across all three looks rather than leaning into silver for her cool colouring. It is good enough to send with light edits, but not yet the bold, quiet surprise this wardrobe could deliver.

results.requestText: It's raining all day and I'll be walking a lot. What should I wear?

looks.title: Sage Set Under the Trench
looks.idea: A tonal sage co-ord under the trench: calm, grown-up and cool-toned, in fabric that breathes in the humidity.
looks.howToWear: Wear the shirt buttoned and half-tucked into the trousers, with the sleeves pushed to the elbow. Cuff the wide-leg trousers twice so the hems stay clear of puddles. Belt the trench loosely, or leave it open if it gets muggy. Keep the crossbody under the trench so the nylon stays dry. The cap brim keeps rain off your face.
looks.why: This is the co-ord you've only worn once, and it suits you: sage is on your palette and the wide leg is a relaxed shape you like. The matching set looks deliberate and more put-together than jeans and a tee. Linen dries fast, and the running shoes make hours of walking comfortable. No black sits near your face.

looks.title: Navy Shirt Dress, Rain Edit
looks.idea: One-piece dressing with a trench: easy, minimal and a step up, with nothing heavy to get soaked.
looks.howToWear: Button the dress to the chest and cinch it with the tan belt at the waist. Roll the sleeves to three-quarter length. Wear the trench open over it and let the navy show as a long column. Wear the Chelsea boots with bare ankles. Carry the leather tote on your shoulder, tucked under the trench if the rain gets heavy. Add the fine chain at the open collar.
looks.why: Navy is a flattering colour for you, and the straight belted shirt dress suits your broad shoulders and slim hips. The tan belt and gold add a bit of interest without being loud. The leather boots keep your feet dry. They're the warmest option, so swap to the running shoes if the humidity wins.

looks.title: Linen Shirt, Shorts and Trench
looks.idea: Your best everyday formula, adapted for a wet day: fresh and easy with no wet hems.
looks.howToWear: Wear the white linen shirt loose and untucked, with the cuffs rolled and the top button undone. Let the mid-thigh denim shorts sit just below the shirt hem. Wear the trench open or belted over the top. Add the chain and watch. Keep the sunglasses in the crossbody for when the rain eases.
looks.why: This is a variation on the white linen shirt and jeans combination that felt effortless for you. Shorts mean nothing heavy and wet clinging to your legs on a humid 21° day. Bare legs dry in minutes. Soft white near your face is flattering, and the trench keeps the look polished rather than beachy.

output.note: All three looks use the trench, because it's your only rain layer. You have no umbrella and no truly waterproof shoes. If you're walking in heavy rain, the running shoes are the safest bet. The white trainers and tan slides would stain and slip, so I left them out. Satin pieces like the cobalt skirt don't suit rain, so save that for a dry day.

failures.detail: s54 black mesh running shoes will be wet through within an hour of walking in all-day rain. The leather Chelsea boots s51 are flat, shed water far better, and look sharper with a wide-leg co-ord and trench.
Double-cuffing soft linen wide-legs (s27) won't hold. They'll unroll and wick water anyway. Better to let them fall to the ankle over a boot, or accept damp hems, because linen dries fast.
The cotton cap s66 soaks through and puts black right at the face. It's a small issue, but it contradicts the stylist's own 'no black near your face' claim.

looks.comment: This is the strongest look and a genuinely good idea. It activates the once-worn sage co-ord (s17/s27) under the trench in a calm, cool-toned COS/Jenni Kayne register that moves her out of black. Swap s54 for s51 and it's finished.

failures.detail: Wearing the trench s44 open 'to show the navy column' undermines the only rain protection she has on an all-day rain day. It should be belted, with the column read through the hem and boots.
The leather tote s60 will water-mark in sustained rain. The nylon crossbody s61 is the rain bag. Bare ankles in Chelsea boots on a long walking day also invite blisters.

looks.comment: Navy shirt dress (s36), tan belt, trench and flat Chelsea boots is a polished, grown-up, on-palette answer that suits her frame, and it rightly uses the most rain-ready shoe. The styling instructions just need to prioritise staying dry over showing the dress.

failures.detail: The logic is wrong on fabric. Wet denim (s28) is exactly the heavy, slow-drying, clinging thing it claims to avoid. A white linen shirt (s07) goes sheer when rained on.
Mid-thigh shorts barely showing below a long shirt, under a knee-length trench, reads as bare legs under a coat. It's an awkward, unintentional silhouette.
This just recycles her known 'worked' formula with shorts swapped in. It's a step backwards from her 'more grown-up, a bit more interesting' aspiration.
Sunglasses s67 on a forecast of rain all day are filler. The mesh s54 shoes repeat Look 1's wet-feet problem.

looks.comment: This is the weak link. The fabrics fight the weather, the proportion under the trench is off, and it regresses to beachy casual when the wardrobe can do far better. I'd cut it.

judgement.missedOpportunity: Replace Look 3 with s08 light blue oversized shirt (loosely tucked) + s30 navy pleated trousers + s44 trench belted + s51 black Chelsea boots + s61 nylon crossbody + s63 gold hoops + s65 watch. It's a tonal blue-and-beige, grown-up look built on her only tailored bottom. The wool blend handles damp better than cotton, it keeps black away from her face, and it puts the most water-resistant flat shoe on a walking day.
judgement.summary: This is a sensible, honest edit. The stylist correctly made the trench the backbone and plainly flagged the missing umbrella and waterproof shoes. Look 1 smartly revives the unworn sage co-ord, and Look 2 is a polished, on-palette navy column. But the shoe advice is inverted: mesh running shoes are not the 'safest bet' in all-day rain, and the leather Chelsea boots (s51) are. Look 3 should be cut, because wet denim, sheer-when-wet white linen and the bare-legs-under-coat proportion fail both the weather and her aspiration. Fix the footwear, keep the trench belted, and swap Look 3 for the navy pleated trouser look.

results.requestText: First date — cocktails at a smart bar.

looks.title: Cobalt Hour
looks.idea: The never-worn cobalt satin skirt finally gets its moment, kept simple with a white tee so the colour does the talking.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the fitted white tee in fully so the bias-cut skirt sits at the natural waist. Drape the cream cardigan over your shoulders, unbuttoned, for the air-con and for a softer line. Wear the fine gold chain at the neckline and the small hoops. Add the silver watch and the silver flats, and keep the crossbody small and worn across the body.
looks.why: Cobalt is one of her flattering cool colours and it sits right by her face in a place that suits her. Satin plus a plain cotton tee is relaxed and minimal, like her COS and Toteme references, but a step up from her usual denim. The silver flats add a bit of interest without volume and keep her on flat shoes.

looks.title: Tonal Tailoring
looks.idea: Navy and dusty blue, sharp but unfussy: her only tailored trousers with an oversized shirt worn loose.
looks.howToWear: Tuck only the front of the oversized light blue shirt into the high-rise pleated trousers so the pleats show. Leave the back loose. Roll the sleeves to just below the elbow and open two buttons, with the gold chain sitting in the V. Add the small hoops and the silver watch, then finish with the black ballet flats and the crossbody.
looks.why: Navy and dusty blue are core colours for her, and the tonal pairing reads as grown-up without trying hard. The wide, straight trouser shape fits her broad shoulders and slim hips and keeps her comfortable. It's polished enough for a smart bar but still feels like her, and it's cool in the humidity.

looks.title: Sage Set, Dressed Up
looks.idea: The under-worn sage linen co-ord, styled as a quiet evening suit rather than a holiday set.
looks.howToWear: Wear the sage linen shirt open as a light jacket over the cream ribbed tank, with the sleeves pushed up to the forearm. Tuck the tank into the wide-leg trousers and cinch the drawstring so the waist is defined. Add the gold chain over the tank, the small hoops, the silver watch, the silver flats and the crossbody.
looks.why: Sage and cream are soft cool-leaning tones that suit her colouring, and she has only worn this set once. Splitting the set into an open shirt layer over a tank turns it from a beach co-ord into something interesting but still understated. It's breathable linen for 24°C and humid weather, with a long, easy line.

output.note: No heels, per her preference for flats outside weddings. I avoided black near her face. The wardrobe's only evening bag options are the large tote and the small black nylon crossbody. A small leather clutch or structured bag would sharpen all three looks.

failures.detail: The rationale says cobalt 'sits right by her face', but s34 is a skirt. The colour is at the hem, not the face. The white tee is what sits at her face, so the colour logic is explained wrongly.

Draping s42 over the shoulders adds bulk across her already broad shoulders. It also brings a preppy, slightly fussy note into an otherwise clean line. Carry it, or wear it properly buttoned, instead.

The s61 black nylon crossbody undercuts satin and silver flats. The stylist did flag this gap honestly. The mixed gold (s63, s64) and silver (s56, s65) metals go unaddressed: one line on why it works was needed.

looks.comment: This is the right instinct: the never-worn s34 against a plain white tee with s56 is exactly the 'more interesting but not loud' upgrade she wants. The fitted s02 is fine, but the s07 white linen shirt (her proven win), tucked with sleeves rolled, would be more relaxed, more grown-up and more her. The cardigan should come off the shoulders.

failures.detail: s30 navy pleated trousers with the s08 light blue poplin shirt is essentially her leadership-review outfit. Nothing in it signals evening or a date, so it reads as coming straight from the office.
Black round-toe s52 is the dullest shoe choice here. The pointed s56 silver flats would give the evening lift and a sharper line. The same s61 nylon crossbody is used again.

looks.comment: The tonal blues are flattering and the front-tuck showing the pleats is good technique. But as a first-date look it has no evening intent and feels like a work uniform. It needs a shift in register, not just jewellery.

failures.detail: It tells her to 'cinch the drawstring' on s27, but s27 has no drawstring listed. The drawstring trousers are s26, so she can't follow the instruction. Calling cream 'cool-leaning' is also a stretch: s13 is warm next to sage, so the stylist should have said why it works anyway.

An all-linen set creases quickly when sitting in humidity. Over a long evening at a smart bar it can slide from 'quiet evening suit' toward rumpled. She should know to expect the crumple and wear it as intentional.

looks.comment: Splitting the s17/s27 set into an open-shirt layer over s13 is a genuinely good reinvention of an under-worn piece. It is breathable for 24°C, and s56 with the gold chain lifts it. It sits at the casual edge of 'smart bar', and the drawstring instruction is simply wrong.

judgement.missedOpportunity: s34 cobalt satin skirt with s07 white linen shirt. Tuck the shirt fully, open two buttons with s64 at the neckline, and roll the sleeves. Add s56 silver flats, s63 hoops, s65 watch and s61 crossbody, and carry s42 for the air-con. This is her proven 'white linen shirt' win, elevated for evening by the never-worn cobalt satin: relaxed, clean, grown-up and quietly interesting.
judgement.summary: The strong part is the wardrobe use: the never-worn cobalt skirt, the once-worn sage set and silver flats, and her only tailored trouser all get a turn. Black stays away from her face and her flats directive is respected. The explanations have factual slips: cobalt 'by her face' when it is a skirt, and a drawstring that doesn't exist on s27. Look 2 is an office outfit with jewellery rather than a date look. The identical accessory stack and nylon crossbody across all three looks flatten the range, although the stylist honestly flagged the bag gap. Look 1 should swap s02 for the s07 linen shirt and lose the shoulder drape. Look 2 needs a real evening move. With those fixes this would be a confident send.

results.requestText: Weekend brunch and then wandering around the shops.

looks.title: Cobalt Satin and a White Tee
looks.idea: The never-worn cobalt skirt dressed down with the simplest white tee, so the colour does the talking.
looks.howToWear: Half-tuck the front of the boxy white tee into the skirt so the waist is defined but the shape stays relaxed. Let the skirt hang loose and bias-cut, no belt. Wear the silver flats with bare ankles. Add the fine gold chain, small hoops and silver watch, and carry the small crossbody across your body to keep your hands free for shopping.
looks.why: Cobalt is one of her flattering colours, and a plain white tee keeps it minimal rather than loud. It is the 'more interesting, but not loud' step she wants. It is also easy: a tee, a skirt and flats, in light fabrics that cope with humidity. The silver flats lift it out of casual without adding heel.

looks.title: Sage Linen, Split Up
looks.idea: The once-worn sage co-ord worn as separate, relaxed pieces so it feels easy rather than matchy.
looks.howToWear: Wear the sage shirt open and untucked over the fitted white tee, with the sleeves pushed to the elbow. Pull the wide-leg trousers up to sit at the waist and let them fall straight over the slides. Carry the straw tote. Keep the jewellery to small gold hoops and the silver watch, and wear the sunglasses.
looks.why: Sage is on her palette and linen is the best fabric for 24°C and humidity. Breaking up the set, with the white tee underneath, makes it look styled rather than like a uniform, and it brings out a piece she has barely worn. The long, relaxed lines suit her broad shoulders and slim hips, and it is very COS and Jenni Kayne.

looks.title: Navy Shirt Dress, Sneaker Edit
looks.idea: A belted navy shirt dress with white trainers: polished enough to look grown-up, easy enough for hours of walking.
looks.howToWear: Undo the top two buttons and roll the sleeves to just below the elbow. Belt the dress with the tan leather belt at the waist and blouse the bodice slightly. Leave the skirt falling straight to the midi length. Wear the white trainers, with the gold chain, hoops and silver watch. Carry the black tote for shopping bags.
looks.why: Navy is a flattering colour for her and keeps the face area soft, unlike black. A shirt dress is one piece and one decision, so it is quick on a weekend morning. The tan belt echoes the tan accent from her successful white shirt look, and the trainers keep it practical for the shops. It is more put-together than jeans and a tee but still clean and minimal.

output.note: Nothing is missing for this brief. Every look uses flats, avoids black near the face, and brings in a piece she rarely or never wears.

failures.detail: s56 pointed metallic ballet flats, worn once, are a gamble for hours of wandering the shops. s53 tan slides or s50 trainers are her proven walking shoes. Bias satin (s34) in humid 24°C will also show sweat and crease, which the stylist doesn't flag.

Gold hoops and chain (s63/s64) are mixed with silver flats and watch (s56/s65) and never explained. On a cool-toned client, silver near the face would be the cleaner choice. It also never considers s07, the white linen shirt from her proven winning look, which breathes better than jersey and adds the polish she's asking for.

looks.comment: This is the right move for the never-worn cobalt skirt (s34): plain white top, colour does the work, and it lands exactly on 'interesting but not loud'. A boxy jersey tee half-tucked into bias satin can bunch at the hip, so s07 tied or tucked would be sharper. Comfort for a long walk needs a second look.

failures.detail: The look is titled 'Split Up' and claims to wear the co-ord 'as separate pieces', but s17 and s27 are worn together. It is the full set with a tee underneath. The rationale contradicts the outfit.

Actually breaking up the set would have been more useful and more teaching. For example, s17 open over s01 with s21 light-wash jeans, or s27 trousers with s01 tucked and s53. That builds new outfits rather than re-wearing the one way she already tried.

looks.comment: Tonal sage linen with a white tee, tan slides and the straw tote is genuinely her: COS / Jenni Kayne, breathable, and good for her proportions. But the stylated idea is mislabelled, and the explanation sells a 'split' that isn't happening. s62 is a beach tote; it works for a casual weekend but is the most holiday-coded choice here.

failures.detail: Shirt dress plus white trainers is competent but familiar. It is the least 'more interesting' of the three, with no real twist beyond swapping in the tan belt (s68).
It doesn't say whether s68 replaces the dress's own belt, or why black (s60) is right with navy and tan. The straw tote (s62) would tie into the tan belt more cleanly for a sunny weekend.

looks.comment: This is the most practical look for brunch and hours on foot: one piece, flattering navy at the face, a tan accent that echoes her winning look, and a tote big enough for purchases. It is grown-up and clean, but it plays it safe.

judgement.missedOpportunity: s34 cobalt satin skirt + s07 white linen shirt (front-tucked, sleeves pushed, collar open) + s53 tan leather slides + s61 crossbody + s65 silver watch + s63 hoops. This brings her proven white linen/tan slide formula to the never-worn skirt. It is cooler in the humidity, more walkable, and more polished than a jersey tee with untested pointed flats.
judgement.summary:
This is a solid, sendable edit. The stylist correctly reached for the under-used colour pieces (s34, s17/s27, s36), kept every look flat and black away from the face, and gave three genuinely different silhouettes.

What holds it back from excellent is mostly precision:
- **Look 2's 'Split Up' framing is simply wrong.** The full co-ord is worn together.
- **Look 1 is under-considered for real life.** It uses once-worn pointed flats for a long walk and satin in humidity, and ignores s07, her proven winner.
- **Metals are mixed without comment** on a cool-toned client.
- **Look 3 is reliable but safe.**

Tighten the explanations and swap the shoes and top in Look 1, and this goes from good to excellent.

results.requestText: I'm presenting to senior leadership next week. I want to look authoritative but still like me.

looks.title: Navy Tailoring, Softened
looks.idea: Her one tailored trouser in a crisp blue shirt: authority through proportion and colour rather than a suit.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the front and sides of the oversized shirt into the high-rise pleated trousers and leave the back looser, so the shape stays relaxed. Undo one extra button and roll the sleeves to just below the elbow. Let the wide straight leg skim the ankle bone over the black flats. Keep the jewellery to the small gold hoops and the silver watch. Carry the tote.
looks.why: Navy and dusty blue suit her cool, low-contrast colouring, with no black near her face. The pleated trousers are the sharpest piece she owns and have only been worn 3 times. The look reads as put-together and grown-up but stays in the COS and Toteme territory she likes: clean, relaxed and minimal. The cotton poplin copes with humidity better than a jacket would.

looks.title: Sage Co-ord, Finally Worn
looks.idea: A tonal soft-green set that looks deliberate and quietly senior, with no effort needed.
looks.howToWear: Wear the set as a true two-piece. Tuck the shirt fully into the wide-leg trousers and loosen the drawstring so it sits flat and the waist looks clean. Leave the top button undone and roll the sleeves once or twice, neatly. Add the fine gold chain at the neckline. Steam the linen the night before so it looks crisp. Finish with the silver pointed flats and the black tote.
looks.why: This is her most under-used piece, worn once, and sage is a flattering colour for her. A single colour head to toe elongates her frame and softens her broad shoulders. Slim pointed silver flats add polish without a heel. It is the 'sharper version of her own style' look: relaxed linen, but one step up from white shirt and jeans.

looks.title: Cobalt Moment
looks.idea: Her never-worn cobalt skirt, with plain white and a blazer to keep it grown-up and a little interesting.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the fitted white tee fully into the bias-cut skirt, so it sits at the high waist and the skirt falls straight. Throw the oversized blazer over the top and push the sleeves up to the forearm so it looks slouchy rather than stiff. Wear the gold chain at the neckline, with the hoops and watch. The silver flats pick up the sheen of the satin. Keep the blazer on for the presentation and take it off when you're out in the heat.
looks.why: Cobalt is one of her best colours and gives the 'bit more interesting, not loud' she wants. White next to her face keeps things fresh, so the black blazer stays below the face and her tired-in-black problem is avoided. The oversized blazer gives her authority and balances her broad shoulders, while the slim satin skirt shows off her slim hips. The skirt has never been worn, and this look makes it work with plain basics she already owns.

output.note: Her wardrobe has only one tailored bottom (s30) and no blazer in a softer cool colour, as the only one is black. A grey or navy blazer would be the one buy that completes this brief. The black blazer is optional over looks 1 and 2 if the room is cold, but 24°C and humid means linen and poplin should do the job without it.

failures.detail: The half-tuck oversized s08 is relaxed, but nothing defines the waist. The tan belt s68 is unused, as is the fine chain s64 that would lift the open neckline. The mixed gold s63 and silver s65 are left unaddressed.
No aircon layer is offered except the black blazer. The cream cardigan s42 over the shoulders would be a softer, on-palette option for a cold boardroom.

looks.comment: This is the right answer to the brief. s30 is her one tailored piece and is under-worn, and s08 keeps cool blues at her face, so she gets authority without a suit and stays in COS/Toteme territory. It is close to her proven white-shirt formula, just stepped up. Ask for a full, neat tuck rather than a front tuck for the presentation itself, and add s64.

failures.detail: Linen s17/s27 will crease after sitting through a morning in humidity, so steaming the night before won't hold until the presentation. Authority comes mostly from the matching, not the fabric.

'Loosen the drawstring so it sits flat' is backwards: a loosened drawstring drops the waist and bunches under a full tuck. The claim that a column 'softens broad shoulders' is overstated, since it elongates but does nothing at the shoulder.

looks.comment: This is a smart use of the once-worn co-ord, and sage is genuinely flattering on her. It reads as deliberate but sits at the softer end of 'authoritative', so it suits a less formal review better than a big exec moment. The styling instruction should be to tie the drawstring flat and tuck the shirt, or wear it loose and untucked with the cuffs rolled.

failures.detail: The black lapels of s40 frame the neck and shoulders. The claim that the blazer 'stays below the face' is false, and black at the shoulder line is exactly what tires her colouring.

The oversized, structured s40 widens her already broad shoulders rather than balancing them. The fitted tee s02 tucked into bias-cut satin s34 clings at the hip and seat, which goes against her preference for relaxed, straight shapes and edges toward the bodycon she rejects.
A polyester-blend blazer kept on at 24°C in humidity will be uncomfortable.
Two of the stated reasons, that the blazer is away from her face and that it balances her shoulders, are visually wrong and would teach her the wrong lesson.

looks.comment: Bringing the never-worn cobalt s34 into a work look is the right instinct and gives her the 'a bit more interesting' she wants. The execution falls back on black and cling. Swap s02/s40 for the light blue s08 or the white linen s07, loosely tucked, for a tonal cool-blue look that is relaxed and more her.

judgement.missedOpportunity: s34 cobalt satin skirt + s08 light blue oversized shirt, tucked neatly with sleeves rolled + s56 silver pointed flats + s64 fine gold chain + s63 hoops, with s42 cream cardigan for aircon. This is a blue-on-blue look that is interesting without being loud and authoritative through its clean line, with no black near the face and no cling.
judgement.summary: This is a strong edit overall. The stylist reached for exactly the right pieces: s30, her only tailoring, the under-used sage co-ord s17/s27, and the never-worn cobalt s34. They also honestly named the missing soft-coloured blazer. Look 1 is ready to send. Look 2 needs its drawstring and tucking instruction fixed and is softer on authority. Look 3 should be restyled before it goes out: the black oversized blazer sits at her face and broadens her shoulders, the fitted tee and bias satin cling, and the explanation defends these with incorrect reasoning. Also standardise the metals or embrace the mix deliberately across all three looks.

results.requestText: Wedding guest — outdoor afternoon ceremony, and the forecast says it might rain.

looks.title: Cobalt Satin Afternoon
looks.idea: The cobalt skirt finally gets its moment, kept quiet with soft cream and minimal gold.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the cream ribbed tank in at the waist so the bias-cut skirt falls straight from the hip. Wear the fine gold chain and small hoops, with nothing else on top. Silver flats pick up the sheen of the satin. Carry the trench over your arm, and belt it loosely if it showers. Wear sunglasses for the ceremony.
looks.why: Cobalt is one of her best colours and it lights up her blue eyes. Cream next to her face is softer than black or stark white. The shape is a straight column with no cling, so it stays relaxed and minimal but looks clearly dressed up. The satin skirt has never been worn, and this is the right occasion for it.

looks.title: Soft Tailoring
looks.idea: Navy wide-leg trousers and a crisp pale blue shirt: grown-up and polished, still easy.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the oversized shirt fully into the high-rise pleated trousers, then pull a little out at the waist so it blouses. Undo two buttons and roll the sleeves to just below the elbow. Add the tan belt, gold hoops, fine chain and silver watch. Wear the black ballet flats. The trench goes over the top for rain.
looks.why: This is her version of COS or Toteme tailoring, in navy and dusty blue, which are both in her palette. The wide, straight trouser suits her broad shoulders and slim hips. It is wedding-appropriate without a dress, and it handles humidity and rain well. The look is also a step up from her usual jeans and tee.

looks.title: Sage Linen Set
looks.idea: A tonal co-ord worn as a deliberate, quiet suit: easy, clean, and a bit more interesting.
looks.howToWear: Wear the set together. Button the shirt, leave the top two open, and tuck it in loosely at the front only. Roll the sleeves once or twice and let the wide-leg trousers sit full length over the flats. Add gold hoops and the fine chain. Steam the linen the night before. If rain is forecast, wear the trench over it on the way in and take it off for the ceremony.
looks.why: Sage is a soft cool colour that flatters her, and the set has only been worn once. It looks deliberate and put-together rather than pieced together. The relaxed wide-leg shape is what she's most comfortable in, and linen is the best fabric for 24°C and humidity.

output.note: The silver ballet flats and black ballet flats are your only suitable flat dress shoes, so the three looks share them. Pick the pair that suits the day. The 8cm stiletto sandals aren't suitable for grass and rain, and they're not a low heel, so I left them out. Your wardrobe has no dressy clutch, so the small black crossbody is the best option, and there's no umbrella. I'd avoid the white broderie dress, since white can compete with the bride, and the black satin pieces, since black near your face looks harsh. A small silver or neutral clutch would round out the wedding looks.

failures.detail: The cream ribbed tank s13 (formality 1/5, slim rib jersey) is a basics layer, not a wedding top. Next to a satin midi it reads as gym-to-brunch. A tucked linen or poplin shirt (s07, s08 or s17) would match the skirt's register.
A slim, thin-strapped tank exposes and narrows the frame around her broad shoulders. She prefers relaxed shapes, and a fuller shirt on top would balance the bias skirt better.
Satin s34 water-spots in rain and on wet grass. The trench helps, but the look doesn't mention this risk, and humidity will make the jersey tank cling.
It calls the bias-cut satin 'a straight column with no cling', but bias-cut satin skims the body by design. That claim is inaccurate and teaches nothing.

looks.comment: Using cobalt s34 at last is the right instinct and the colour is perfect on her. But the cream tank undercuts it. Swap in a tucked shirt with the sleeves rolled and this becomes the hero look.

failures.detail: The navy pleated trousers s30 with the light blue shirt s08 is her leadership-review outfit. Nothing marks it as a wedding, so it looks like she came straight from the office.
The tan belt s68 sits against black flats s52 and a black nylon bag s61, so the leathers fight. The silver flats s56 would have tied in with the silver watch s65 and lifted the look.
It says the look 'handles humidity well', but wool blend with cotton poplin at 24°C humid is the warmest, least breathable option of the three. Linen would outperform it.

looks.comment: It is competent and in her palette, but it's a workwear answer to a celebration brief. The pieces are right for a COS-style wedding suit, yet the styling never steps it up from Tuesday.

failures.detail: Linen spots and creases when wet. Telling her to wear the trench s44 belted, rather than just 'on the way in', would protect the steamed finish if it showers during the ceremony.

looks.comment: This is the strongest look: the never-worn sage co-ord s17/s27 worn as a soft suit is exactly Jenni Kayne and sits right in her cool palette. The silver pointed flats s56 sharpen it, and the linen is right for 24°C and humid.

judgement.missedOpportunity: Cobalt satin skirt s34 with the light blue oversized poplin shirt s08 (or the white linen shirt s07, her proven success), tucked and bloused with the sleeves rolled. Add silver flats s56, small gold hoops s63, silver watch s65 and the trench s44. Tonal blues light up her eyes, the relaxed shirt balances her shoulders, and satin against crisp cotton gives the 'grown-up but interesting' Toteme effect.
judgement.summary: The stylist found the right under-used pieces (s34, s17/s27, s30, s56) and was honest about the gaps: no clutch, no umbrella, and no suitable low heel. Look 3 is ready to send. Look 1 has the best idea but the wrong top: the cream tank undercuts the satin skirt. Look 2 is office tailoring with mismatched leathers. Looks 2 and 3 are both shirt-plus-wide-trouser, which narrows the range. Rework Look 1 with a shirt and restyle Look 2 with the silver flats and a less work-coded top before this goes out.

results.requestText: How should I wear my cobalt satin midi skirt (s34)?

looks.title: Cobalt, Kept Easy
looks.idea: Let the skirt be the one bold note against the crisp white basics she already wears all the time.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the front of the boxy white tee into the skirt, leaving the back loose, so the waist is defined and the boxy shape stays. Wear the skirt high on the waist so it falls straight and long. The white trainers keep it casual, so the satin reads as relaxed rather than dressy. Add the gold hoops, silver watch and sunglasses, and carry the crossbody.
looks.why: It's close to her white tee and jeans formula, with the skirt in place of the jeans. White next to cobalt looks clean and suits her cool, low-contrast colouring. The satin gives her a more grown-up, interesting piece without any fuss, and it works as a first, low-risk way to wear it for office days or brunch.

looks.title: The Linen Shirt, Dressed Up
looks.idea: Her proven white linen shirt and tan slides formula, with the skirt replacing jeans for a fresher weekend look.
looks.howToWear: Roll the linen sleeves to the elbow and tuck the shirt loosely into the skirt, with a soft blouse at the waist. Leave the top two buttons open and let the fine gold chain sit in the V. Wear the tan slides and carry the straw tote. The matt linen against the satin gives a nice contrast in texture.
looks.why: This repeats what has already worked for her: white linen shirt, tan slides, an easy and fresh feel. The skirt lifts it from jeans to something a bit more considered. Linen is breathable in 24°C humidity, and the flat sandals suit a weekend brunch or beach day.

looks.title: Blue on Blue
looks.idea: A tonal take that looks polished and quiet, with light blue poplin against deep cobalt.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the oversized light blue shirt fully into the skirt, then pull it out a little for a soft blouse. Roll the sleeves just below the elbow and leave the collar open. Wear the silver ballet flats and carry the black tote. Keep the jewellery minimal with the gold hoops and the silver watch.
looks.why: Dusty and light blues are in her best colour range, and the tonal pairing feels deliberate without being loud. The oversized shirt suits her broad shoulders, and the flats keep it practical and comfortable. It's her most put-together option for a leadership review or presentation, and the black blazer (s40) can go over it if the office aircon is cold.

output.note: No heels are needed. The skirt works with her flat shoes and basics. All three looks avoid black near her face. Her black blazer (s40) is the only outer layer I'd add for formal days, but it's too warm to wear in the 24°C humidity. A pale grey or navy top would be a useful addition to her wardrobe for wearing with the skirt.

failures.detail: Satin skirt + white tee + white trainers is the stock answer to this question. It is right as a first wear, but nothing here is particular to Sarah beyond the fact that she owns s01 and s50.

A front-tuck of a hip-length boxy cotton tee (s01) into a bias-cut satin skirt will bunch at the waist and drag the bias line. A short front knot, or a tight tuck then a slight blouse, would keep the satin falling clean.

looks.comment: A sound, low-risk entry point. White against cobalt is crisp and kind to her cool, low-contrast colouring, and the trainers stop the satin reading as dressy. It does the job but has no point of view beyond 'swap the jeans'.

failures.detail: Pitches this for a 'beach day'. Satin is the wrong fabric for sand and salt spray. This is a brunch look.
The tan leather belt (s68) would connect the tan slides (s53) and the straw tote (s62) at the waist. It would also neatly hide the bulk from tucking linen into satin.

looks.comment: The best look here. It builds on her proven s07/s53 formula. Matt linen against fluid satin, plus warm tan and straw against cobalt, gives the 'a bit more interesting, not loud' she asked for. It overlaps in colour story with Look 1, since both are a white top with the cobalt skirt.

failures.detail: Two problems with the reasoning. First, it suggests the black blazer (s40) over the look for aircon, contradicting both the stylist's own 'no black near her face' rule and their note that it's too warm. Second, it says the oversized shirt 'suits her broad shoulders', but a dropped-shoulder oversized shirt (s08) adds width there rather than balancing it.
A fully tucked oversized poplin shirt in a bias satin skirt creates volume at the hip. Her slim hips can carry it. A roll at the waistband, or a half-tuck, would keep the skirt's line long.

looks.comment: A good tonal idea in her best colour family, and it puts the near-unworn silver flats (s56) to real use. That is the smartest wardrobe pull in the set. The polish of a leadership-review look is let down by muddled layering advice and mixed metals: gold hoops (s63) beside silver shoes and a silver watch.

judgement.missedOpportunity: After-work drinks, the evening register she clearly needs and none of the three looks covers. Build it from: cream ribbed tank (s13) tucked into the cobalt skirt (s34), cream knit cardigan (s42) over the shoulders, silver ballet flats (s56), fine gold chain (s64), silver watch (s65), with the trench (s44) for the walk home. Two smaller misses: a navy-tee tonal day look (s05 + s34 + s50), and a soft grey-marl version (s03), since the stylist wrongly claims she lacks a grey or navy top.
judgement.summary:
These are competent, wearable looks. All are flat-soled, weather-appropriate and kind to her cool colouring, and Look 2 is genuinely strong. The weaknesses are as follows.

- **Overlapping looks:** Two of the three are 'white top + cobalt skirt'.
- **No evening look:** Nothing covers after-work drinks or night, though the satin skirt is naturally suited to it.
- **Errors in the note:**
  - It recommends a pale grey or navy top as a new purchase when she already owns s03 and s05.
  - It offers the black blazer despite its own black-at-face rule.
- **Missed tweaks:** Tucking technique into bias satin is under-thought, and the tan belt (s68) is left unused.

Send it after fixing the note and swapping Look 1 or 3 for an evening option.

results.requestText: Long travel day tomorrow — I want to be comfortable but still look put-together.

looks.title: Sage Linen Set, Travel Edition
looks.idea: A tonal sage co-ord that looks planned, not thrown on, and is as comfortable as loungewear.
looks.howToWear: Wear the sage shirt open like a light jacket over the white fitted tee, with the front hem of the tee loosely tucked into the drawstring waist. Roll the shirt sleeves to just below the elbow. Keep the trousers full length and let them skim the top of the trainers. Carry the cream cardigan in the tote for the cold cabin and drape it over your shoulders at the gate. Add the gold hoops and silver watch, nothing else.
looks.why: This is your most under-worn piece (worn once), and it's ideal for a long day: breathable in 24° humidity, with loose linen that won't dig in after hours of sitting. Sage is one of your flattering cool colours, and the matching set reads polished while you're still in easy, straight shapes. Linen will crease, but on a travel day that looks relaxed and intentional. White trainers handle airport walking.

looks.title: Soft Tailoring, Zero Effort
looks.idea: Wide navy trousers with a white tee and a pale blue shirt: quietly grown-up and still easy.
looks.howToWear: Tuck only the front of the white boxy tee into the high-rise pleated trousers so the waist is defined and the trousers sit properly. Wear the light blue oversized shirt open over the top with the sleeves pushed up. Wear the fine gold chain at the neckline. Keep the trainers clean and white, and put your passport and essentials in the tote so your hands stay free.
looks.why: The navy pleated trousers are your only tailored bottom and have only been worn three times. The wide, straight cut is as comfortable as jeans but looks much more put-together. Navy, white and pale blue are all flattering cool tones near your face, with no black to tire you out. The open shirt gives you an extra layer for the air-con, and the whole look stays in the clean, minimal COS/Toteme space you like.

looks.title: The Easy Shirt Dress
looks.idea: A navy shirt dress with tan accents: one piece, nothing to coordinate, and a bit more interesting than jeans.
looks.howToWear: Button the dress to the sternum and leave the lower buttons open for stride room. Swap the dress's own belt for the tan leather belt, worn at the natural waist and not too tight, so you can sit comfortably. Wear the denim jacket on your shoulders or put it on for the cold cabin. Wear the crossbody across your body for hands-free airport moves, and add the gold hoops and chain. The tan slides slip off easily at security. If you'll be doing a lot of walking, swap to the white leather trainers (s50).
looks.why: A single piece in breathable cotton is the most comfortable option in humid heat, and the midi length looks composed after hours in transit. Navy with tan and denim echoes the effortless feel of your white shirt, jeans and tan slides combination, which has worked for you before. The belt and gold jewellery add the sharper, grown-up detail you're after without being loud.

output.note: I don't know where you're flying to, so I've kept every look layered for cold cabins and 24° humidity. If the destination is cooler, the cream cardigan or black leather jacket would be good additions. I left out the cobalt satin skirt for this brief: it's a lovely piece but better saved for after-work drinks or a wedding-guest outfit than a long-haul day.

failures.detail: The fitted tee s02 tucked into a drawstring waist is less forgiving over hours of sitting than the boxy tee s01. s01 also matches her stated preference for relaxed, straight shapes better.

looks.comment: This is the right answer for the brief. The never-styled sage co-ord (s17/s27) is in her best colour family and in breathable linen, worn open as a jacket over a white tee so it reads planned rather than pyjama. The cardigan in the tote handles the cabin, and the stylist was honest about creasing; the black tote s60 is the only heavy note, and it is the only practical bag she has.

failures.detail: s30 has a fixed high-rise waist and pleats, in a wool blend. It will crease at the lap and press on the stomach on a long-haul sit, and wearing her only tailored bottom on a travel day risks wrecking it.
Calling s30 'as comfortable as jeans' does not hold up for a travel day. The note also never deals with wool blend in 24° humidity.
This is the same formula as Look 1: open shirt over a white tee, wide trousers, white trainers, black tote, hoops and watch. Only the colour changes.

looks.comment: Navy, white and pale blue (s30/s01/s08) is a flattering, grown-up palette that fits the COS references. But it is the least travel-practical of the three trousers she could have worn and repeats Look 1's structure. It would be better presented as an arrival or meeting look than as the travel-day option.

failures.detail: The tan slides s53 should not be the default for a long travel day: they mean bare feet in a cold cabin and are poor for long gate walks or a rushed connection. The trainer swap s50 should lead, not sit as a footnote.
The small nylon crossbody s61 won't hold a cardigan, water and snacks, and the denim jacket s41 is bulky to carry. Pairing it with the tote s60 would cover a full travel day.

looks.comment: The navy shirt dress s36 with the tan belt s68 swapped in is a nice, specific styling move. The look also sensibly echoes her proven white shirt, jeans and tan slides formula. For travel it needs the trainers and a bigger bag; a belt and an open-button midi are also slightly more to manage in a plane seat than trousers.

judgement.missedOpportunity: none. Look 1 is the wardrobe's best travel answer. It would be sharper with the boxy tee s01 swapped in for s02 and the light blue shirt s08 kept in the tote as an alternative cabin layer to the cardigan.
judgement.summary: This is a good set that avoids black near her face, activates under-worn pieces and respects the flats directive. Look 1 (the sage co-ord) is genuinely strong and should lead. Look 2 is attractive but repeats Look 1's formula and puts a fixed-waist wool-blend tailored trouser on a long-haul day. Look 3 works but defaults to slides and a tiny bag where trainers and the tote would serve her better. The note about saving the cobalt skirt is sensible.

results.requestText: What should I wear to work tomorrow?

checks.detail: Shares most of its clothing with look 1.
Shares most of its clothing with look 2.

looks.title: Black-out cargo
looks.idea: Head-to-toe black utility: the easiest way to meet the café's plain-black rule on a bike in the cold.
looks.howToWear: Wear the band tee inside out so the print drops to a faint ghost and it reads close to plain black. Keep it untucked and boxy over the cargos, with the legs worn straight over the boots. Put the cropped puffer on for the ride and leave it in the staff area. The tote carries the rest.
looks.why: The cargos are the only plain black bottom that works with a full day on the bike. They are warm, they won't catch the wind, and they keep her undone, streetwear shape with the boxy tee over relaxed legs and chunky boots. The cropped puffer is the warmest layer she has for 4°C and wind, and it stays off at work.

looks.title: Slip and boots
looks.idea: A black satin slip dress roughed up with tights and chunky boots: Berlin club-kid sharpness for a shift behind the counter.
looks.howToWear: Wear the opaque tights under the slip dress with the lace-up boots, and the silver chain at the neck. Before cycling, knot the hem at one hip or tuck a handful of fabric into the tights so the bias cut doesn't flap in the wind, then release it at work. Pull the puffer over the top and zip it fully. The thin straps and satin will be cold on the ride without it.
looks.why: The slip is the only fully plain black piece that is a complete outfit, so it satisfies the dress code best. Pairing soft satin with heavy boots and a chunky chain is the 90s grunge and club mix she wears well. The 80 denier tights and the puffer cover the 4°C ride. The hem knot keeps it safe to cycle in.

looks.title: Tee over slip
looks.idea: A faded band tee thrown over the slip dress: a 90s grunge layer, mostly black, with the music showing.
looks.howToWear: Layer the boxy, faded band tee over the slip dress so the satin hem hangs out below it. Knot the tee at the side if the hem needs shortening for the bike. Wear the tights and boots, add the chain over the tee neckline, and zip the puffer on top for the ride.
looks.why: It is her style balance of an oversized top against something fitted and short, and the tee is the piece she wears most. The mix of cotton and satin looks undone rather than polished. It is mostly black, with only the print breaking it up. The tights, boots and puffer keep her warm on the walk and cycle.

output.note: Her wardrobe has no plain black top, and the café dress code is plain black. The band tee is the closest piece, and it is best worn inside out (look 1) or under a slip dress, which will be mostly plain black. Check whether the café supplies an apron or a uniform top. If not, a plain black tee or long-sleeve top would be the most useful buy, as it would make the cargo look fully compliant and cheaper to repeat.

failures.detail: No styling nod to her music or grunge side beyond the tee's ghost print. Wearing the l14 chain to and from the shift, or tucked under the neckline, would keep it her without risking the dress code.

looks.comment: This is the right answer to the brief. The l06 cargos, inside-out l02 tee, l11 boots and l10 puffer give a fully black, cycle-proof, wind-proof outfit. Turning the tee inside out is a clever, honest workaround for a wardrobe with no plain black top, and the seams-out finish suits her undone style.

failures.detail: The l08 satin slip with thin straps leaves her arms bare for a whole November café shift. Satin also water-spots and shows coffee splashes badly. It meets the dress code but is evening wear doing day-job duty.
Knotting or tucking a bias-cut midi for the bike is a workaround rather than a solution. Doing it twice a day plus at the café is fiddly.
Calls satin-plus-boots 'the mix she wears well', but l08 has only 3 wears and nothing in her history supports this. The 'Why' also skips the obvious fix of a sleeved layer underneath.

looks.comment: Good club-kid idea and correctly plain black, but it's a night-out look moved onto a shift behind the counter. With an inside-out l02 underneath for sleeves it would have been workable; as written it's cold and fragile for work.

failures.detail: The l02 band print is worn facing out, which breaks the café's plain-black rule. The stylist turned the same tee inside out in look 1 to solve exactly this, then abandoned the fix here.

Calls this her 'oversized top against something fitted and short', but l08 is a midi. The tee-over-slip shape is long-over-long, not her stated balance. The explanation also admits the print breaks the plain black instead of fixing it.
A boxy tee over a bias midi with a side knot for cycling creates a lumpy, bunched middle under a cropped puffer. It reads unresolved rather than intentionally undone.

looks.comment: A nice grunge reference, but as a work outfit it fails the one hard rule of the brief. It also mostly repeats look 2's slip, tights, boots and puffer base.

judgement.missedOpportunity: Slip dress l08 layered over black cargos l06, with the band tee l02 worn inside out underneath. Add l11 boots, l10 puffer, l14 chain for after the shift, and l15 tote. It is fully black for the café and gives sleeves for warmth. Trousers under the slip remove the bike-hem problem entirely. Slip-over-trousers on top of a tee is pure Berlin club and 90s layering, a stronger second look than either slip option offered.
judgement.summary: Look 1 is a confident, honest, practical answer, and the stylist's note flagging the missing plain black top is exactly the kind of candour a client needs. The other two looks lean on the same slip dress and add little range. Look 2 is cold and fragile for a café shift. Look 3 drops the dress-code fix the stylist had already found. One strong look plus two variants that needed more thought about the actual job.

results.requestText: Dinner with friends at a nice restaurant on Saturday night.

looks.title: Slip Dress, Undone
looks.idea: Satin slip dress roughed up with a cropped puffer and chunky boots, the 90s grunge way to dress up.
looks.howToWear: Wear the white ribbed tank under the slip dress so the tank straps and neckline peek out, a layered 90s look that also adds warmth. Put the black tights on underneath, then the lace-up boots, with the midi hem skimming the top of the boot shaft. Wear the cropped puffer open so the dress falls long below it, which keeps the proportion short over long. Let the silver chain sit over the tank and slip neckline. Carry the tote.
looks.why: This is the dressiest thing she owns, and it gets there through texture contrast rather than polish, so it doesn't turn corporate. The black, white and silver palette suits her high-contrast colouring. The bias-cut dress, opaque tights and chunky boots are fine to cycle in, and the puffer handles the cold wind on the ride.

looks.title: Tartan and Forest
looks.idea: Her favourite gig formula (oversized top, tartan mini, tights, boots) turned up a notch for dinner by swapping the hoodie for the green knit.
looks.howToWear: Tuck only the front of the chunky green jumper into the tartan skirt and let the back hang loose, which keeps the oversized top balanced against the short skirt. Wear the black opaque tights and lace-up boots, and push the jumper sleeves up to the forearm. Put the vintage leather jacket over the top, left open, with the silver chain sitting on the knit neckline.
looks.why: It repeats what has worked for her in spirit: a big top, a short A-line skirt, tights and boots. The deep green and red both suit her colouring. The wool knit, wool skirt and tights are warm enough for 4°C. It is the most comfortable look for walking and cycling, and the tartan and leather jacket keep it vintage-grunge rather than neat.

looks.title: All Black, Brown Leather
looks.idea: Black-on-black band tee and cargos, with the vintage leather jacket adding warmth and a dressed-up undone feel.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the boxy band tee fully into the cargo trousers to define the waist, and let the relaxed leg fall over the top of the boots without bunching. Wear the leather jacket on the shoulders with the collar up, and layer the silver chain over the tee so it is visible. Carry the tote.
looks.why: It is the most casual of the three and the closest to her Berlin club style. The tonal black and the faded music tee give the head-to-toe darkness she likes, and the brown jacket adds vintage warmth. On the windiest ride swap the leather jacket for the black puffer, as the tee is only a light layer. It is easy to cycle in.

output.note: Her wardrobe has no dressy shoes or smart layers, but that suits her style, so dinner is handled through texture, layering and the slip dress rather than polish. If the restaurant is properly dressy, Look 1 is the safest choice.

failures.detail: A bias-cut satin midi (l08) is not 'fine to cycle in' as stated. It rides up, twists and can catch, and needs gathering or knotting at the side to ride. The cropped puffer (l10) also leaves satin-and-tights legs exposed to the 4°C wind on the bike. It is workable, but this should have been addressed rather than waved through.
Indoors, with the puffer off, she is in thin straps over a tank in a November restaurant. An option to throw l04 or l09 over it at the table would have helped.

'Midi hem skimming the top of the boot shaft' is inaccurate. On 167cm a midi lands mid-calf, well above an ankle boot. The visible strip of opaque tight between hem and boot is part of the look and should be described honestly.

looks.comment: This is the right anchor and the right idea. The dressiest piece is made hers through the l03 tank underneath, the l11 boots and the l10 cropped puffer, and short-over-long works for her frame. It needs an honest cycling note: knot or gather the hem to ride.

failures.detail: Front-tucking a chunky cable knit (l04) into an A-line wool mini (l07) bunches bulk exactly at the waist and hip. Her proven formula works because the hoodie hangs over the skirt. Leave the jumper untucked so only a band of tartan shows below it.

Cable knit plus red tartan mini drifts towards preppy schoolgirl or festive red-and-green, which is the one direction she says betrays her. The l14 chain and l11 boots rescue some of it, but the styling needs to push harder towards undone.

Push-up sleeves are cosmetic under a hip-length leather jacket (l09), since you can't push them up inside it. The brown jacket over a voluminous knit also bulks at the arms. Little thought went into how the outer layer actually sits.

looks.comment: Taking the gig formula up a notch with the green knit is a sensible, client-specific move, and it is the warmest look for the conditions. The tuck and the preppy risk keep it from feeling sharp.

failures.detail: Band tee (l02) and cargos (l06) are her everyday studio and café uniform. Nothing here marks 'dinner at a nice restaurant on Saturday night'. It is a filler look.
A single cotton tee under a hip-length leather jacket in a 4°C cold wind on a bike is genuinely cold. The 'swap to the puffer' fix is admitted in the text but not built into the look.
Wearing the leather jacket 'on the shoulders' cannot be done while cycling or walking in wind. It is a static editorial pose, not real-life styling.
'Dressed-up undone feel' is asserted, not shown. Nothing in the look is dressed up.

looks.comment: Tonal black with a band tee is on-brand but answers no brief beyond 'leaving the house', and it is underlayered for the weather. The same base with l04 in place of the tee would at least be warm and a step up.

judgement.missedOpportunity: Black satin slip dress (l08) with the oversized forest green chunky jumper (l04) worn loose over it, the bias-cut satin falling long beneath. This is her own 'oversized top over something fitted' rule and the most 90s grunge way to dress the dress up. Finish with black opaque tights (l13), lace-up boots (l11), the chain (l14) and the vintage leather jacket (l09) or cropped puffer (l10). It is warmer than Look 1, has deep green at the face and satin-vs-cable texture contrast, and is more rideable with the knit on top.
judgement.summary: Look 1 is a genuinely good, on-brand answer to a dressy brief from a casual wardrobe, though its cycling claim is too breezy. Look 2 is a reasonable evolution of her proven gig outfit, but the front tuck and cable-knit-plus-tartan pairing pull it towards bulky and slightly preppy. Look 3 is a weak filler: everyday clothes, underlayered for 4°C wind, with an impractical shoulder-drape. The stylist's note about lacking dressy shoes and smart layers is fair and honest. The edit needed a second idea that uses the slip dress, or the green knit with trousers, instead of a default tee-and-cargos.

results.requestText: Surprise me — put together something I wouldn't normally think of.

looks.title: Satin Under Fleece
looks.idea: Soft slip dress under a scruffy hoodie: the satin-against-sweatshirt mix of Berlin club style.
looks.howToWear: Pull the grey hoodie on over the slip dress and leave it loose, so the satin midi hem drops 15cm or more below the hoodie hem. Put the opaque tights on under the dress and lace the boots tight. Wear the cropped puffer on top, so you get three hems stacked at different lengths: puffer, then fleece, then satin. Let the hood sit outside the puffer collar and wear the chain over the hoodie. If the dress flaps while you cycle, hitch it up a little through the hoodie. The tights and boots keep your legs covered.
looks.why: The slip dress has only been worn 3 times, and this makes it an everyday piece instead of a going-out one. Oversized on top with a fluid, narrow shape underneath is the balance you like. It also draws on your grunge references, with the slip over a hoodie as a 90s move. The hoodie, tights, boots and puffer keep it warm for 4°C and wind, and the boots and tights make it safe for walking and cycling.

looks.title: Tartan, Turned Down
looks.idea: Red tartan and forest green in an undone, scruffy mix that looks like a worn-in 90s band tee and not a Christmas outfit.
looks.howToWear: Pull the chunky green jumper on loose and tuck only a small section at the front into the mini skirt, so the back and sides stay bulky. Wear the black tights and the retro green and white trainers, which pick up the green of the jumper. Put the boxy leather jacket on open and let the jumper hem hang out under it. Wear the chain over the jumper neckline, and shove the tote on a shoulder or hang it off the handlebars.
looks.why: The tartan skirt is under-worn at 6 wears and is your best piece for gigs. Red and deep green both suit your high-contrast colouring. The trainers, the scruffy leather jacket and the loose, partly tucked jumper stop it reading as festive or preppy. The big jumper over a short skirt gives you the oversized-over-short proportion you like. The jumper is the warmest piece you own, and with tights and a leather layer it holds up against the wind.

looks.title: Tank Over Tee
looks.idea: A slim white rib tank pulled over a faded band tee, with low-slung jeans, for an inside-out take on layering.
looks.howToWear: Put the boxy band tee on first, then pull the slim white tank over it. The tank should hug the body, with the black tee sleeves and the bottom hem showing around it, and the graphic partly visible. Wear the baggy jeans low and roll the hems once or twice so they sit above the chunky boot soles and stay clear of the bike chain. Put the cropped puffer on over everything with the chain outside it, and zip it to the chin against the wind.
looks.why: Layering the tank over the tee gives you a fitted shape over a boxy one, with a dark and light contrast that suits your colouring, and it looks like something you'd do on purpose. The band tee keeps the music-led side of your style, and the light-wash jeans lift the otherwise black outfit. It stays warm and bike-friendly, because the puffer, boots and rolled hems cover you for walking and cycling.

output.note: Your wardrobe has no scarf, beanie or gloves. At 4°C with a cold wind, those would help most on the bike, and any of them would fit with all three looks.

failures.detail: A bias-cut satin midi (l08) on a bike is a real chain-snag risk, and 'hitch it up through the hoodie' is a hope rather than a fix. The legs are also only in 80-denier tights (l13) under thin satin at 4°C with wind. A knot or side-tie at the hem would be safer, and a note to save this for walking-heavy days would help.

looks.comment: This is the genuine surprise the brief asked for. It moves the 3-wear slip dress (l08) into daytime by putting it under the most-worn hoodie (l01), and the stacked hems of cropped puffer (l10), then fleece, then satin are a deliberate Berlin-club proportion. The only weak spot is the satin hem on a bike.

failures.detail: In mid-November, red tartan (l07), forest green (l04) and green-and-white trainers (l12) push this towards festive. Choosing trainers that 'pick up the green' makes the matchiness worse, not better. The black boots (l11) would break the colour echo and keep it grunge.

Low-top suede trainers (l12) plus an open leather jacket (l09) on a bike in a cold 4°C wind leave the ankles and the front of the body exposed. Zip the jacket while riding, and the boots would be warmer.
The idea line ('looks like a worn-in 90s band tee') doesn't make sense for an outfit with no band tee in it. The explanation also never admits this is close to her existing favourite gig outfit.

looks.comment: This is a near-repeat of her proven formula, with the jumper standing in for the hoodie (l01) and trainers for the boots, so it is only a mild surprise for a 'surprise me' brief. The brown leather (l09) adds a nice vintage note, but the green-on-green-on-red risks Christmas, which is exactly what the stylist says it avoids.

failures.detail: Take away the tank (l03) and this is her everyday uniform: band tee (l02), baggy jeans (l05), boots (l11), puffer (l10). With the puffer zipped to the chin outdoors, the only new idea disappears exactly when she's out in it.
Low-slung jeans (l05) under a cropped puffer (l10), leaning forward on a bike in a cold wind, leave a gap at the lower back. The torso warmth is also only two thin cotton layers under the puffer.
Tank-over-tee reads more early-2000s trick than grunge. The look reaches for it while ignoring stronger untouched pieces such as the cargo trousers (l06).

looks.comment: This is competent and wearable, but it's the least surprising look of the three. The one styling move is hidden under a zipped puffer, so it lives mostly indoors at the studio.

judgement.missedOpportunity: Slip dress over cargos: the black satin slip (l08) worn over the black cargo trousers (l06), with the forest green jumper (l04) pulled on top, plus the black boots (l11), cropped puffer (l10) and chain (l14). The cargos remove both the cycling-hem problem and the cold-legs problem while keeping the satin surprise. The green jumper puts deep green at the face for her high-contrast colouring, and the cargo trousers, unused in all three looks, finally get worn.
judgement.summary: Look 1 is genuinely excellent and does exactly what 'surprise me' asks: it makes the under-worn slip dress part of daytime life in a way that fits her grunge and Berlin club references. Looks 2 and 3 fall off. Look 2 is mostly her favourite gig formula re-coloured, with a festive red-and-green risk the shoe choice makes worse, and practical gaps for a bike in the wind. Look 3 is her daily uniform with a layering trick hidden under a zipped puffer. The cargo trousers are never used, even though they are the obvious tool for making the slip dress bike-proof. The note about missing hat, scarf and gloves is honest and useful.

results.requestText: It's raining all day and I'll be walking a lot. What should I wear?

looks.title: Rainy Studio Day
looks.idea: The undone hoodie-and-cargo uniform, sealed against the weather by boots and a puffer.
looks.howToWear: Wear the oversized hoodie under the cropped puffer and pull the hood out over the puffer collar to keep rain off your neck. Leave the hoodie hem long so it peeks below the cropped puffer. Pull the cargo hems over the top of the boots so water runs off instead of in, or tuck them in if it's pouring. Wear the silver chain over the hoodie. Carry the tote close under your arm or inside your jacket line, as canvas soaks through.
looks.why: Cargos are the right call in cold rain: twill dries faster than denim and the hems won't drag. The oversized top over a short puffer fits your preferred proportions, and the black boots and puffer keep it grungy. It's easy to cycle in and has plenty of pockets for a day on the move.

looks.title: Tartan and Green
looks.idea: Your gig-night formula, swapped for a warmer top that makes red and deep green work together.
looks.howToWear: Pull the chunky green jumper loose over the tartan mini, with the hem sitting mid-hip and a little skirt showing beneath. Add the opaque tights and the lace-up boots, then the cropped puffer on top, left open so the green and red show. Wear the chain over the knit neckline.
looks.why: It follows the spirit of your favourite outfit: oversized top, short skirt, tights, boots. The wool jumper and skirt give real warmth at 3°C, and red and deep green are both strong colours on you. The short skirt keeps the oversized knit balanced, and tights plus boots keep you covered and warm on the bike.

looks.title: Slip and Tee Grunge
looks.idea: A 90s grunge layer of satin slip over a band tee, made weatherproof with tights and boots.
looks.howToWear: Wear the faded band tee under the slip dress, so the boxy sleeves and hem show at the neckline and the boxy shape sits under the bias cut. Add the opaque tights and boots, then the puffer zipped over everything. Wear the silver chain over the tee. If cycling, let the midi skirt fall over the saddle and keep the puffer closed against wind.
looks.why: This is the most night-ready look: satin against faded cotton and chunky boots is classic Berlin club and grunge. The tee and tights add warmth to a dress that would otherwise be too thin for November. It's a different route to your style, built on mixing soft and rough.

output.note: Your leather jacket and the suede-and-leather trainers aren't used because both would be ruined or soaked in all-day cold rain. The puffer is your only real weather layer, so it appears in every look. Jeans are skipped because wet hems at 3°C get cold and heavy. Missing from the wardrobe: a waterproof shell or umbrella and a rain-proof bag, as the canvas tote will get wet.

failures.detail: Pulling the cotton-fleece hood of l01 out over the puffer collar means it will soak in all-day rain and wick cold water to the neck; better to keep it inside and use it only under a hat. Missed layering l13 tights under l06 cargos as a thermal base for 3°C.
Carrying the large l15 tote 'inside your jacket line' doesn't work under a cropped puffer. Better advice: line it with a plastic bag.

looks.comment: The right answer for the day. l06 cargos, l11 boots and a zipped l10 puffer handle walking, cycling and rain, and the long hoodie hem under the cropped puffer is exactly her oversized-plus-short proportion. The hood advice is backwards for cotton fleece in rain, and a tights base layer would have made it genuinely warm.

failures.detail: The l10 puffer is told to be 'left open so the green and red show'. In 3°C rain all day, that soaks the l04 wool knit and l07 wool skirt, and it stays wet and heavy. Legs in only l13 tights will be wet and cold for hours of walking.
A cable-knit forest green jumper over a red tartan mini tips towards preppy or schoolgirl-Christmas, which she has named as a betrayal. The chain and boots only partly rescue it.
It claims the wool gives 'real warmth at 3°C' without addressing that wet wool and wet tights are the opposite of warm.

looks.comment: A sensible riff on her proven gig formula, but it is styled for a dry evening, not a rain-soaked walking day. The open-puffer instruction actively undermines the brief. As a dry-day outfit it might pass; here it doesn't.

failures.detail: The l08 satin midi hangs well below the cropped l10 puffer and will water-mark and cling cold and wet all day. Legs are protected only by l13 tights.
Cycling in a bias-cut satin midi in the rain is workable but fiddly, with a wet saddle and fabric near the chain. Delicate satin, worn only 3x, is the wrong piece to sacrifice.
With the puffer zipped over the tee-under-slip layering, the satin-versus-cotton idea is hidden. All you see is black puffer over a black wet skirt.
It is pitched as 'most night-ready', which isn't the brief. It also contradicts the note that rejects l09 and l12 for being ruined by rain.

looks.comment: A genuinely good grunge idea in the wrong forecast. Satin in all-day 3°C rain is exactly what the stylist's own note warns against, and the zipped puffer hides the idea anyway.

judgement.missedOpportunity: A second rain-proof trouser look instead of two skirt looks: l13 tights worn under l06 cargos as a thermal layer, l03 tank under the l04 forest green jumper (deep green at the face), l10 puffer zipped, l11 boots with cargo hems over the shafts, l14 chain over the knit, and l15 tote lined with a plastic bag. It is warm, dries well, works on the bike, and is different from Look 1 through colour and texture.
judgement.summary: Look 1 is sound and the stylist's note is honest about what the wardrobe lacks: no shell, no umbrella, no waterproof bag. The correct exclusions of l09, l12 and l05 show real-life thinking. But Looks 2 and 3 abandon the brief. Both put her in wet tights for an all-day walking rain. Look 2 tells her to leave the only weather layer open, and Look 3 sacrifices a satin slip to the rain while the note warns against exactly that kind of damage. With a fixed puffer-boots-tote-chain shell across all three, variety should have come from weather-sound bases, such as a cargo-and-green-knit look with a tights base layer, not from night-out skirt looks.

results.requestText: First date — cocktails at a smart bar.

looks.title: Slip and Leather
looks.idea: Black satin slip against beat-up leather: the dressed-up look that still feels like her.
looks.howToWear: Wear the slip dress over the 80 denier tights with the chunky boots so the satin looks edgy, not precious. Put the leather jacket on over it and leave it unzipped with the sleeves pushed up slightly. Wear the chain at the neckline. The puffer goes over everything for the cycle and comes off at the bar. Keep the tote for your things.
looks.why: It's the most date-ready option in her wardrobe, and the slip dress has only been worn 3 times. Satin with worn leather and chunky boots keeps it grunge, not polished. The bias-cut midi works on a bike with tights underneath, and the boots and puffer cover the 4°C wind.

looks.title: Green Knit, Red Tartan
looks.idea: Deep green and red on a short skirt: her gig-night formula, turned up for a date.
looks.howToWear: Pull the oversized green jumper on over the tartan mini, tucking only the front few centimetres of hem so the skirt peeks out under the knit. Add the opaque tights and lace-up boots. Wear the chain over the knit's neckline. Wear the puffer for the ride and take it off inside.
looks.why: It follows the shape of her favourite gig outfit: oversized top, short tartan skirt, black tights, boots. Forest green and red both flatter her high-contrast colouring. The big knit against a short skirt is the proportion she likes, and the wool and tights keep her warm on the bike. It uses the tartan skirt, which she's worn only 6 times.

looks.title: Cargo Night
looks.idea: Relaxed black cargos with a bare white tank and leather: low-key Berlin, with the skin and chain doing the date work.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the white ribbed tank into the cargos, leaving the waistband slightly slouchy. Put the leather jacket on open over it. Wear the chain over the tank so it's visible. Wear the retro white and green trainers with the cargo hems stacked at the ankle. Wear the puffer over everything for the cycle and take it off at the bar.
looks.why: This is the easy, undone option. The fitted tank balances the baggy trousers, and the white against black leather is sharp on her colouring. The trainers are the most comfortable shoe for a long cycle. It's the least dressy of the three, but the chain and clean tank make it look deliberate.

output.note: Her wardrobe has nothing truly smart, which suits her style anyway. The slip dress look is the most dressed-up. If the bar is strict about trainers, choose look 1 or 2, which both have boots.

failures.detail: Layering the cropped puffer l10 over the boxy leather jacket l09 is bulky, and the cropped puffer leaves her lower back and hips exposed to a 4°C wind on the bike. Inside the bar she then has two jackets to stash in the canvas tote l15. Choosing one outer layer, or the knit l04 under the puffer, would be cleaner.

There is no instruction for cycling in a bias-cut satin midi: it rides up and clings to 80-denier tights l13. She should knot the hem or clip it to one side for the ride. The canvas tote l15 also reads heavy for a cocktail bar, though it is the only bag she owns.

looks.comment: This is the right anchor. The slip l08 is under-worn, black satin against brown vintage leather l09 is genuine 90s grunge, and the chunky boots l11 keep it hers rather than polished. It needs a smarter answer to the double jacket and the bike.

failures.detail: A front tuck of chunky cable knit l04 into an A-line wool mini l07 creates bulk right at the waist. A full drop with the skirt hem just showing, or a sleeve push to show wrist, would be cleaner. The chain l14 also gets lost against the cable texture.

This is essentially her gig outfit with the hoodie swapped for a jumper. It is comfortable and on-brand, but it is not stepped up for a smart bar. The leather jacket l09 or a white tank l03 collar peeking at the neck would have lifted it.

looks.comment: Green and red tartan on her high-contrast colouring is a real, flattering pairing, and it is warm and fine on the bike. It reads 'nice gig night', though, not 'first date at a smart bar'.

failures.detail: Cargos l06, a ribbed tank l03 and trainers l12 make an everyday studio outfit with a chain added. Calling it date-ready on the strength of 'skin and chain' does not make it so for a smart cocktail bar.

Low-top trainers l12 and a single thin rib tank are cold choices for cycling into a 4°C wind. The boots l11 would solve both the ankle chill and the stylist's own 'if the bar is strict about trainers' worry. Swap them in rather than leaving it as a caveat.
The stylist admits it is the least dressy and hedges in the note, but never says why it belongs in a smart-bar brief at all.

looks.comment: This is the weakest look. It is plausible Berlin, but under-pitched for a first date at a smart bar and chilly in the trainers. With boots and the tank layered under the slip dress, it would have been a different and better look.

judgement.missedOpportunity: Forest green chunky jumper l04 worn loose over the black satin slip dress l08, so the satin hem shows below the knit. Add black tights l13, lace-up boots l11, the chain l14 at the neck and the cropped puffer l10 for the ride. It is 90s grunge, warm enough for 4°C, dressier than the tartan look, and puts her best colour (deep green) at the face. Alternatively, put the white ribbed tank l03 or band tee l02 under the slip for the classic grunge layer.
judgement.summary: The stylist found the right hero piece in the under-worn slip dress l08, and Look 1 is a confident, on-DNA date look, though the double-jacket layering and cycling in a satin midi needed solving. Look 2 is warm and flattering but stays at gig-night level rather than date level. Look 3 is under-dressed for a smart bar, and trainers in a 4°C wind is a choice the stylist hedged on instead of fixing. The strongest move, oversized green knit over the satin slip, was left on the table.

results.requestText: Weekend brunch and then wandering around the shops.

looks.title: Green Knit, Cropped Puffer
looks.idea: Cosy oversized knit against baggy denim, with the green picked up again in the trainers.
looks.howToWear: Wear the jumper loose and let the hem hang over the low-slung jeans. The cropped puffer sits just above the knit hem so you get a layered, stepped shape. Stack the chunky chain over the jumper's neckline. Roll the jeans once to show the trainers and keep the hems off the chain when you cycle. Put the tote across your body for the bike.
looks.why: This is her oversized-with-something-short balance: a big jumper under a cropped puffer. Forest green is one of her best colours against black hair and fair skin. The knit and puffer together handle 4°C and the wind. The green on the trainers ties the look together without being matchy. Everything is comfortable for the bike and for hours of shop wandering.

looks.title: Gig Skirt, Brunch Edition
looks.idea: Her favourite hoodie, tartan and boots formula, with the leather jacket added for wind.
looks.howToWear: Wear the hoodie big with the hem falling over the skirt waistband, so only the tartan hem shows. Put the leather jacket over the top and pull the hood out over the collar. Wear the opaque tights under the skirt and lace the boots tight. Wear the chain outside the hoodie, over the drawstrings, and carry the tote.
looks.why: This is the outfit she has already proved she loves, with a layer for the weather. The oversized hoodie against the short skirt is her ideal proportion. The red tartan suits her colouring. The tights and boots keep her warm and make the skirt fine for the bike. The vintage leather jacket adds the grunge edge and blocks the wind.

looks.title: Slip Over Tee
looks.idea: A satin slip layered over a faded band tee, grungy and music-led, kept warm with a puffer.
